name: Matter Status Bot

parameters.content:
## Matter Status Bot

### How it works

1. The workflow triggers on incoming client queries via SMS webhook or email read.
2. It parses incoming messages and identifies clients by matching phone numbers or email addresses with Clio contacts.
3. For identified clients, it checks cooldown periods to avoid repeated rapid replies.
4. It retrieves open matter statuses from Clio and composes status replies.
5. The workflow runs compliance checks before sending replies via SMS or email, respecting client opt-outs.
6. If no client match is found, it sends a "client not found" reply via the relevant channel.

### Setup steps

- - [ ] Configure Twilio credentials for SMS send and webhook receive functionality.
- - [ ] Set up IMAP email credentials for reading incoming client emails.
- - [ ] Configure SMTP or email send credentials for sending email replies.
- - [ ] Provide Clio API base URL and authentication credentials as environment variables.
- - [ ] Import and set the compliance check sub-workflow referenced in the execution.
- - [ ] Ensure the cooldown logic is properly implemented to avoid multiple rapid responses.

## SMS inbound trigger and parse

Webhook trigger on incoming SMS and parsing its contents.

## SMS client lookup by phone

Query Clio contacts by phone and confirm client match.

## SMS client match decision

Check if client identified by phone and branch accordingly.

## SMS cooldown check and matter fetch

Check SMS reply cooldown to prevent flooding or repeated replies.

## SMS matter status retrieval and compliance

Fetch matter status from Clio and verify compliance before texting back client.

## SMS send or skip reply

Send status SMS reply if allowed; otherwise skip if client opted out.

## Email inbound trigger and parse

Trigger on incoming emails and parse status request content.

## Email client lookup by email

Query Clio contacts by email and confirm client match.

## Email client match decision

Check if client identified by email and branch accordingly.

## Email cooldown check and matter fetch

Check email reply cooldown to avoid multiple quick responses.

## Email matter status retrieval and compliance

Fetch matter status for email and run compliance checks before email response.

## Email send or skip reply

Send status email reply if allowed; otherwise skip if client opted out.

nodes.name: When Client Sends Status Text
nodes.notes: Point your Twilio number's 'A message comes in' webhook at this URL. Responds immediately; the actual reply goes out separately via the Twilio send node below.

nodes.name: Parse Incoming Status SMS
nodes.notes: Twilio's inbound-SMS webhook posts form-encoded fields — From and Body are what matter here.

nodes.name: Fetch Clio Contact By Phone
nodes.notes: Clio's own contact search handles partial/formatted phone matching reasonably well; verify against a real number on first live test since exact matching behavior can vary by how numbers are stored.

nodes.name: Match Client Using Phone Number
nodes.notes: Matches on the last 10 digits so formatting differences (+1, dashes, spaces) don't cause a false miss.

nodes.name: If Client Found By Phone
nodes.notes: True continues to look up their matters; false means the number doesn't match any Clio contact.

nodes.name: Build Phone Client Not Found Reply
nodes.notes: A generic, non-client-specific message — deliberately doesn't reveal whether ANY client uses this number, just that this exact number isn't recognized.

nodes.name: Fetch Open Matters By Phone
nodes.notes: Only Open matters are reported — a client asking about a closed matter gets pointed to their attorney rather than a stale status.

nodes.name: Build Matter Status SMS Reply
nodes.notes: The actual status text — only facts already in Clio, never advice or predictions.

nodes.name: Check SMS Compliance Before Reply
nodes.notes: Runs the client through the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33) before anything sends — opt-out respected, required disclaimer appended, send logged, same as every other client-facing send in this catalog.

nodes.name: If Approved To Send SMS Reply
nodes.notes: Mirrors the guardrail's approved/opted-out result — true sends the reply, false means the client has opted out of texts.

nodes.name: Send Matter Status SMS Reply
nodes.notes: Reaches back to 'Build Matter Status Reply' by name, not $json, since the guardrail call in between replaces $json with its own response.

nodes.name: Skip SMS - Client Opted Out
nodes.notes: The client's opt-out is respected even for a status reply they themselves requested — texting them anyway would defeat the point of an opt-out.

nodes.name: Send Phone Client Not Found SMS
nodes.notes: This one bypasses the guardrail deliberately — it's a generic 'we couldn't find you' message with no client-specific content, sent to whoever just texted in.

nodes.name: When Client Emails Status Request
nodes.notes: Watches a dedicated inbox (e.g. case-status@yourfirm.com) via IMAP. Credential: Credentials → New → IMAP → your mailbox's server/login details.

nodes.name: Parse Incoming Status Email
nodes.notes: Pulls the sender's address and subject line out of the IMAP-read email.

const from = ($json.from && $json.from.value && $json.from.value[0] && $json.from.value[0].address) || $json.from?.text || '';
return { json: { from_email: String(from).toLowerCase().trim(), subject: $json.subject || '', is_valid: !!from } };

nodes.name: Fetch Clio Contact By Email
nodes.notes: Same contact search as the SMS branch, keyed on email instead of phone.

nodes.name: Match Client Using Email Address
nodes.notes: Exact email match, since email addresses don't have the same formatting variance phone numbers do.

nodes.name: If Client Found By Email
nodes.notes: True continues to look up their matters; false means the address doesn't match any Clio contact.

nodes.name: Build Email Client Not Found Reply
nodes.notes: Same generic non-client-specific message as the SMS branch's not-found reply.

nodes.name: Fetch Open Matters By Email
nodes.notes: Same open-matters lookup as the SMS branch.

nodes.name: Build Matter Status Email Reply
nodes.notes: Same status-only reply logic as the SMS branch, formatted for email.

nodes.name: Check Email Compliance Before Reply
nodes.notes: Runs the client through the Bar-Compliance Guardrail before anything sends — opt-out respected, disclaimer applied, send logged.

nodes.name: If Approved To Send Email Reply
nodes.notes: Mirrors the guardrail's approved/opted-out result for the email branch.

nodes.name: Send Matter Status Email Reply
nodes.notes: Reaches back to 'Build Email Matter Status Reply' by name, not $json, since the guardrail call in between replaces $json with its own response.

nodes.name: Skip Email - Client Opted Out
nodes.notes: The client's opt-out is respected even for a status reply they themselves requested.

nodes.name: Send Email Client Not Found Reply
nodes.notes: Bypasses the guardrail deliberately — generic 'we couldn't find you' message with no client-specific content.

nodes.name: Check SMS Reply Cooldown
nodes.notes: STATUS_REPLY_COOLDOWN_MINUTES controls how long to wait before replying to the same client again — defaults to 5 minutes, so rapid double-texts only get one reply.

nodes.name: Check Email Reply Cooldown
nodes.notes: STATUS_REPLY_COOLDOWN_MINUTES controls how long to wait before replying to the same client again — defaults to 5 minutes, so rapid double-texts only get one reply.

nodes.name: If Within SMS Reply Cooldown
nodes.notes: True means this number already got a status reply within the cooldown window — skips straight to a no-op instead of fetching matters and texting again.

nodes.name: Skip SMS - Recently Replied
nodes.notes: No re-text sent — the client already got a status reply within the cooldown window.

nodes.name: If Within Email Reply Cooldown
nodes.notes: True means this address already got a status reply within the cooldown window — skips straight to a no-op instead of fetching matters and emailing again.

nodes.name: Skip Email - Recently Replied
nodes.notes: No re-reply sent — the client already got a status reply within the cooldown window.

description: Runs on two independent triggers. SMS: a client texts the firm's number, the bot matches their phone number to a Clio contact, looks up their open matter(s), and texts back the current status through the Bar-Compliance Guardrail. Email (separate): same idea over a dedicated IMAP inbox. Never gives legal advice, predictions, or next-steps guidance -- only reports the matter's own status field as recorded in Clio (ABA Op. 512). Replaces standalone case-status apps, freeing attorneys from answering routine 'what's happening with my case' interruptions.
